records.issue_text: eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees call is not wrapped in try/catch, so if it throws after prisma.booking.update already persisted new attendees, the mutation fails for the client while DB and calendar end up inconsistent with no rollback
records.rationale: The diff shows prisma.booking.update persisting new attendees, then `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` unwrapped (while sendAddGuestsEmails IS wrapped in try/catch, showing the author's awareness of external call failures). If updateCalendarAttendees throws, attendees remain in DB, client gets error toast, and calendars are inconsistent — a verifiable consistency defect.

records.issue_text: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, the error message template literal is always a non-empty string, so the || t("unable_to_add_guests") fallback never triggers even when err.data/err.message are undefined, producing a message like "undefined: undefined"
records.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` — a template literal is always a non-empty string, so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` never falls back; if err.data/err.message are undefined, users see 'undefined: ...'. The fallback is dead code and the intended error message never shows.

records.issue_text: The catch block for sendAddGuestsEmails discards the actual error and uses console.log instead of a proper logger/console.error, making email delivery failures unobservable
records.rationale: The diff verifiably contains `} catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` in addGuests.handler.ts — the caught error object is discarded and only a generic message is logged, so email delivery failures (which are silently swallowed) leave no diagnostic trace. This is accurate, specific to new code in this diff, and decision-relevant for shipping (observability of a non-critical failure path), though it is a quality concern rather than a behavioral defect since the operation otherwise succeeds.
